declared_purpose: Create, automate and manage Browserbase cloud browser sessions, preserve authentication across sessions, capture screenshots, record sessions, solve CAPTCHAs and support cleanup. Recording and CAPTCHA solving are explicitly enabled by default; context writeback and keep-alive are optional. These declared features are distinct from implementation choices such as coupling logging to recording. Sources: SKILL.md:3–19,62–68; README.md:11–21.

data_operations.operation: Install dependencies through documented setup commands
data_operations.data_scope: Browserbase and Playwright packages and Chromium browser artifacts.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local installation locations selected by the installers; artifact suppliers are not specified.
data_operations.condition: The documented pip/uv and Playwright installation commands are run. Installer behavior is outside the supplied implementation.

data_operations.operation: Read credentials locally; document optional credential persistence
data_operations.source: Manager environment helpers and credential setup instructions
data_operations.data_scope: BROWSERBASE_API_KEY; BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID for setup, context/session creation and termination.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Manager process memory. Documentation alternatively places credentials in skills.entries.browserbase-sessions.env in ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json; the manager does not implement that configuration write.
data_operations.condition: Commands requiring these variables run. list-contexts only reads the local alias map.

data_operations.operation: Authenticate remote control requests
data_operations.source: Browserbase client initialization and direct context-deletion request
data_operations.data_scope: API credential, operation parameters and applicable project, session or context identifiers.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Browserbase API; the reference identifies api.browserbase.com/v1 and X-BB-API-Key authentication. SDK internals are not supplied.
data_operations.condition: A remote command runs. delete-context constructs the authenticated HTTPS request directly.

data_operations.operation: Read, persist, resolve and list local context aliases
data_operations.data_scope: Friendly context names and Browserbase context IDs. Names can identify sites or workflows; cookies are not written to this file.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: contexts.json under BROWSERBASE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.browserbase; list/create results go to caller stdout.
data_operations.condition: Named context creation saves the map; context resolution and listing read it. Unrecognized input passes through unchanged as the context identifier.

data_operations.operation: Create a persistent cloud context
data_operations.data_scope: Project ID sent to create a context; returned context ID, project ID and optional local name.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Context created at Browserbase; result returned to caller stdout. Authentication state is supplied through later browser use, not uploaded by this command.
data_operations.condition: create-context runs; its friendly name is saved locally only when --name is provided.

data_operations.operation: Attach saved authentication state and optionally persist changes
data_operations.data_scope: Context ID and persist flag; cookies and browser storage delegated to Browserbase. README additionally claims session-storage persistence.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Browserbase browser context and persistent cloud context. The reference states contexts never expire.
data_operations.condition: --context-id attaches a context. --persist requests writeback on close; it defaults to false and has no effect without a context ID.

data_operations.operation: Request cloud-context deletion and remove local aliases
data_operations.data_scope: Resolved context ID and API credential; matching name-to-ID entries.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: DELETE request to api.browserbase.com/v1/contexts/{context_id}; successful handling rewrites the local alias map without matching entries.
data_operations.condition: delete-context runs and the request succeeds or the handled response is HTTP 204. Documentation calls cloud deletion permanent; backend erasure is not independently established.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve session inventory during setup
data_operations.data_scope: Every session object yielded by client.sessions.list(); returned fields and provider-side scope are unspecified.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Browserbase response materialized in local process memory. Inventory contents are not included in successful setup output.
data_operations.condition: setup reaches its API-connection check after environment and import checks.

data_operations.operation: Run a live setup smoke test
data_operations.source: cmd_setup session creation, navigation and cleanup
data_operations.data_scope: Project ID, new session ID, CDP connection information, navigation to example.com and returned page title.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Browserbase API and cloud browser; example.com receives the navigation. Session ID, title and step results return to caller stdout.
data_operations.condition: setup passes earlier checks. CAPTCHA solving is explicitly enabled; recording/logging flags are omitted. Release is attempted after navigation, including navigation failure; release failure produces a warning.

data_operations.operation: Create cloud sessions with configurable collection and lifetime
data_operations.data_scope: Project/context IDs, persistence preference, CAPTCHA setting, viewport, region, proxy, ad blocking, timeout and keep-alive options. Requests session video and logs by default; logs may contain timestamps, methods and params.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Browserbase session infrastructure and recording/log facilities. Returned session metadata, connect_url and conditionally selenium_remote_url/signing_key go to caller stdout.
data_operations.condition: create-session runs. CAPTCHA solving can be explicitly disabled. Without --no-record, record_session and log_session are true; --no-record omits both flags rather than setting them false. Keep-alive/proxy options are sent only when selected; supplied truthy timeouts are bounded to 60–21600 seconds.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve and return session metadata
data_operations.data_scope: Session/context IDs, status, timestamps, region and keep-alive state; get-session additionally returns CPU, memory and proxy-usage metrics obtained from the service.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Browserbase responses enter local memory; selected fields return to caller stdout. These are operational metrics, not locally inferred personal attributes.
data_operations.condition: list-sessions retrieves an unfiltered iterable and applies --status locally. get-session retrieves the supplied session ID.

data_operations.operation: Request session release
data_operations.data_scope: Session ID, project ID and REQUEST_RELEASE status; possible context writeback established when the session was created.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Browserbase lifecycle API; confirmation returned to caller stdout.
data_operations.condition: terminate-session runs. This requests termination, not deletion of recordings, logs or persistent contexts.

data_operations.operation: Connect local Playwright to a remote browser
data_operations.data_scope: Session ID, retrieved connect_url and CDP browser commands/results. Fallback connection URL contains BROWSERBASE_API_KEY and session ID as query parameters.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Browserbase API for retrieval, then the returned CDP endpoint; fallback recipient is connect.browserbase.com. Commands use the first available browser context and page.
data_operations.condition: navigate, screenshot, execute-js or get-cookies runs. A context/page is created if absent. Connection errors return exception text to the caller.

data_operations.operation: Navigate the cloud browser and return page metadata
data_operations.data_scope: Requested URL, browser navigation state and returned final URL, title and HTTP status. Authentication use is delegated to the browser context.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Browserbase cloud browser and the requested site's destination; metadata returns through CDP to caller stdout. Page-dependent additional recipients are unresolved.
data_operations.condition: navigate runs with --url and --session-id.

data_operations.operation: Extract page-body text and truncate the caller result
data_operations.data_scope: Entire cloned body text after removing script, style and noscript elements; local output keeps the first 50000 characters plus a truncation/total-length marker when needed.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Complete extracted text crosses from the cloud page through CDP into local process memory; capped text returns to caller stdout.
data_operations.condition: --extract-text is supplied. Text extraction is not performed by ordinary navigation alone.

data_operations.operation: Capture and persist screenshots
data_operations.data_scope: Rendered viewport, or the full scrollable page when requested; screenshot output path and page metadata.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Screenshot bytes saved to the caller-specified local file through Playwright; paths and metadata return to caller stdout.
data_operations.condition: navigate includes --screenshot, or screenshot runs with --output. --full-page expands capture beyond the viewport. These paths show writes, not automatic file deletion.

data_operations.operation: Execute caller JavaScript and echo its source and result
data_operations.data_scope: Complete --code string, its evaluation result and session ID. Code may contain form values; the documented login workflow uses this command to fill and submit forms.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Code executes in the Browserbase page through CDP; both code and result return to caller stdout. Further reads, writes or transmissions depend on the supplied script.
data_operations.condition: execute-js runs. Browser close and Playwright stop are attempted afterward.

data_operations.operation: Read and return all cookies from the selected browser context
data_operations.data_scope: All cookies returned by context.cookies(), including cookie values and metadata, plus their count; no URL/domain filter is supplied.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Existing cloud browser state crosses CDP into local memory and caller stdout. The command does not write a cookie file or send cookies to another website.
data_operations.condition: get-cookies runs against the context selected by _connect_playwright.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve a recording and persist a local copy
data_operations.data_scope: Recording response content, a returned recording.url, raw bytes or a stringified fallback response; output path and file size.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Retrieval from Browserbase; the URL branch additionally fetches the service-returned URL, whose scheme and host are unspecified. Bytes are written to the requested local output file; only save metadata returns to stdout.
data_operations.condition: get-recording runs. Documentation requires prior termination, but the command does not check session status. No automatic sharing or file deletion is implemented here.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve logs, materialize entries and return a capped subset
data_operations.data_scope: All entries yielded by the SDK response, projected to timestamp, method and params; alternatively a stringified response. Output contains total materialized count and at most 200 entries.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Browserbase response enters local process memory; capped log content returns to caller stdout.
data_operations.condition: get-logs runs. The 200-entry cap applies after enumeration and materialization, not to the API request.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve and return live connection information
data_operations.data_scope: debug_connection_url, ws_url and page IDs, URLs and favicon URLs.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Browserbase debug API response to caller stdout. This command returns URLs without opening those URLs or fetching favicons.
data_operations.condition: live-url runs for the supplied session ID.

data_operations.operation: Return exception text and HTTP error bodies
data_operations.source: Shared JSON output helpers and command exception handlers
data_operations.data_scope: Exception strings and, for failed context deletion, the decoded HTTP error body. Their runtime contents are unknown.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Caller stdout; no separate remote error-reporting destination is shown.
data_operations.condition: An applicable command fails. These handlers do not redact exception/body content before output.

potential_excess.data_scope: Session inventory yielded by client.sessions.list(), beyond information needed to establish that the required smoke-test session can be created.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local setup-process memory receiving Browserbase session objects; not successful setup stdout.
potential_excess.condition: setup reaches its standalone API-connection check.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Setup explicitly requires credential/API validation and a live create/navigate/terminate test. Enumerating existing sessions is an implementation choice and a potentially redundant action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Validate credentials, SDK, Playwright and API access; create, navigate and release a test session.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use the required session-creation request to establish API connectivity instead of separately retrieving existing sessions.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep useful API/authentication diagnostics and the complete live smoke test, including cleanup attempts.

potential_excess.data_scope: Session logs, including method parameters whose actual contents are unspecified.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Browserbase session-log collection/storage requested through browser_settings.log_session.
potential_excess.condition: create-session runs without --no-record, even when only video recording or browsing is needed.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Default video recording is explicitly declared. Automatically enabling log_session alongside recording is an additional implementation choice; log retrieval is a separate supported feature.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Preserve default session recording and make logs available when the workflow requires them.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Control logging separately and request it only for workflows needing logs, while retaining the declared recording default.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: First establish whether Browserbase recording requires log_session and what omission means. That dependency is unresolved in the supplied source.

potential_excess.data_scope: Extracted body-text characters beyond the existing 50000-character output limit.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Cloud-page-to-local-process CDP boundary and local process memory.
potential_excess.condition: navigate --extract-text processes a page whose extracted text exceeds 50000 characters.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Text extraction is requested, but the implementation returns only a capped prefix. Transporting the omitted suffix is extra data within a required extraction action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Return the same text prefix, filtering behavior, total length and truncation marker.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Compute the length and truncate inside page.evaluate, returning only the prefix and length to Python.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve script/style/noscript removal, text fallback behavior, the 50000-character limit and the existing output format.

potential_excess.data_scope: Duplicate JavaScript source, potentially including embedded login or form values.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: The code field in caller stdout; no additional external recipient is established.
potential_excess.condition: execute-js runs without a task requiring its source to be echoed.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Executing JavaScript and returning its result serve browser automation. Repeating the complete source in the response is an extra field in the required action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Transmit and evaluate the requested code, then return status, session identification and evaluation result.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit the code field by default or expose it through an explicit diagnostic option.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep evaluation and result semantics unchanged; retain source echo when explicitly needed.

potential_excess.data_scope: Projected log payloads beyond the first 200 entries retained solely before producing the capped response.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: The local log_entries list in process memory; this is transient retention, not a demonstrated disk write.
potential_excess.condition: get-logs receives an iterable yielding more than 200 entries.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The command returns only 200 entries and a total count. Counting all entries does not require retaining every projected payload.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Preserve the first 200 entries, their order and the count of all yielded entries.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Count entries while retaining only the first 200 projected entries.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve current JSON output and non-iterable fallback behavior. This reduces local materialization; it does not establish reduced upstream retrieval.

unknowns: Browserbase SDK, Playwright and installer implementations are absent. Their additional networking, telemetry, defaults and resolved versions cannot be established; requirements specify lower bounds only (scripts/requirements.txt:1–2).

Downstream CAPTCHA-solving and proxy recipients, page-dependent network recipients, and the actual hosts in service-returned connect_url or recording.url remain unresolved (scripts/browserbase_manager.py:329–372,520–527,548,693–698).

Whether log_session is necessary for video recording is unknown. --no-record omits recording/logging flags, and setup omits them too; service defaults therefore block a firm conclusion about collection on those paths (scripts/browserbase_manager.py:168–171,346–348).

Exact persisted storage fields, including README's session-storage claim, are delegated to Browserbase. The reference says contexts never expire, but actual retention, backups, deletion completion and recording/log retention after release or context deletion are not supplied (README.md:12–13; references/api-quick-ref.md:53–72).

SDK pagination, API inventory scope and upstream filtering/limit support are unspecified. list-sessions --status filters after retrieval; the get-logs output cap does not limit retrieval (scripts/browserbase_manager.py:418–434,724–743).

Runtime URLs and JavaScript are not supplied. Their additional disclosures, state changes or deletions cannot be enumerated. No personal-attribute inference is implemented explicitly; external inference remains unknown (scripts/browserbase_manager.py:548,630).

The remote lifecycle effect of browser.close() after CDP commands is unspecified. Explicit REQUEST_RELEASE can fail, and setup treats cleanup failure as a warning; release is not evidence of erasure (scripts/browserbase_manager.py:193–210,480–491,584–592).

Caller handling of stdout, local artifact retention and eventual sharing destinations are unspecified. Returning cookies, connection credentials, debug URLs or results does not itself establish disclosure beyond the caller. Runtime exception text may contain sensitive details, but actual contents are unknown (scripts/browserbase_manager.py:86–93,278–293,375–407,625–769).
